question.problem:
The dimensions of a package in the shape of a rectangular solid are $0.9\,\text{m}\times 0.9\,\text{m}\times 1.2\,\text{m},$ where each dimension was measured to the nearest $0.1\,\text{m}.$ Rounded to the nearest tenth of a cubic meter, what is the upper bound for the volume of the package?

To the nearest tenth of a cubic meter, the upper bound for the volume of the package is
{{field-1}}${\text{m}}^{3}.$
question.worked_solution:
Each dimension is given to the nearest $0.1\,\text{m}.$ So, the greatest possible error of these measurements is

$$
\frac{0.1\,\text{m}}{2}=0.05\,\text{m}.
$$

We wish to find the *upper bound* for the volume of the package. Therefore, we require the *upper bound* of each dimension.

The upper bounds for each dimension are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & 0.9\,\text{m}+0.05\,\text{m}=0.95\,\text{m} \\  & 0.9\,\text{m}+0.05\,\text{m}=0.95\,\text{m} \\  & 1.2\,\text{m}+0.05\,\text{m}=1.25\,\text{m}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the upper bound for the volume of the package is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =0.95\,\text{m}\times 0.95\,\text{m}\times 1.25\,\text{m} \\  & =1.128\,125\,{\text{m}}^{3} \\  & ≈1.1\,{\text{m}}^{3},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest tenth of a cubic meter.
